newsitem.title: USA: New video evidence surprises O.J. Simpson lawyers.
newsitem.headline: New video evidence surprises O.J. Simpson lawyers.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's lawyers were caught off-guard at his civil trial on Tuesday by a video they tried to suppress that could damage their claim that evidence was planted to frame Simpson for murder.
Video footage clearly showing a gap in dense foliage above the fence next to where a bloody glove was found on Simpson's estate was introduced by the plaintiffs' lawyers and shown to the jury.

The prosecution in Simpson's criminal trial last year contended the former football star murdered his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman on June 12, 1994 outside her home. They suggested Simpson drove back to his nearby estate and climbed over a fence to avoid detection, dropping a bloody glove that matched one at the murder scene.

The spot where they contended he climbed the fence was adjacent to the bedroom of house guest Brian "Kato" Kaelin, who testified he heard three thumping sounds that night that might have been someone bumping into the air conditioner.
Simpson was acquitted of the murders in October 1995 but is being sued for monetary damages for "wrongful death" in civil court by the victims' families.

The introduction of the video taken by Gary Randa, son of Simpson's personal secretary Kathy Randa, appeared to take the defence by surprise and they opposed it being shown. After a lengthy conference in which Simpson lawyer Robert Baker could be heard declaring angrily "Will you let me finish?" Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki allowed the video segment into evidence.

Retired Detective Philip Vannatter testified on Monday that when he observed the bloody glove in a narrow walkway behind Simpson's mansion hours after the murders he saw no evidence that anyone had come over the fence. He also said dense foliage growing by the fence had not been disturbed.

But the Randa videotape, apparently shot a week after the murders when police were again searching Simpson's property, showed a spot behind Kaelin's room where there appeared to be a large gap in the foliage at the top of the chain-link fence.

Vannatter said he was shown the glove by Detective Mark Fuhrman minutes after he had discovered it the morning after the murders. Simpson's criminal defence accused Fuhrman of planting the glove to frame the former athlete.

After seeing the hole in the foliage on the video, Vannatter, being cross-examined by Brown family attorney John Kelly, said he could not have seen that area from his vantage point as he looked at the glove.

Baker interrupted to demand Fujisaki strike Vannatter's testimony from the record and admonish the jury to ignore what they had seen on the video. "You will hold your judgment on this photograph (sic) in abeyance," the judge told the panel.
Existence of the video was not known until Kathy Randa mentioned it when she was deposed for the civil trial by attorneys in June. It was subpoenaed by plaintiffs' attorneys.
